sentences.text: In some testing situations some interface(s) to the SUT may be missing or unknown a priori (e.g. management interface) but it may be necessary that the SUT is stimulated to carry out certain actions (e.g. send a message to the test system).
Also certain actions may be required from the test executing personnel (e.g. to change the environmental conditions of testing like the temperature, voltage of the power feeding, etc.).
The action statement provides the means to write one or more log items e.g. to some displaying device.
Items to be displayed shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the action statement.
Items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such items.
External actions can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
There is no specification of what is done to or by the SUT to trigger this action, only an informal description of the required action itself.
No specific restrictions in addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 and shown in table 16.

requirements.subject: ent:action-statement
requirements.canonical: The `action` statement provides the means to write one or more items, e.g. to a displaying device.
requirements.original: The action statement provides the means to write one or more log items e.g. to some displaying device.

ambiguity.issue: The items of the action statement are called "log items" although they belong to the action statement, not the log statement.

requirements.subject: ent:action-item
requirements.canonical: An item to be displayed by the `action` statement SHALL be identified in a comma-separated list in the argument of the `action` statement.
requirements.original: Items to be displayed shall be identified by a comma-separated list in the argument of the action statement.

requirements.subject: ent:action-item
requirements.canonical: An item of the `action` statement MAY be an individual language element specified in table 18 or an expression composed of such items.
requirements.original: Items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such items.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax (25-s006) only allows FreeText or TemplateInstance, while table 18 (log statement) also lists elements such as timers, ports and component references; it is unclear whether all table 18 elements are allowed in `action`. Chosen reading: the elements of table 18 are allowed.
readings: An item of the `action` statement MAY be any language element listed in table 18 or an expression composed of such elements.
An item of the `action` statement MAY only be a free text or a template instance, as given by the syntactical structure.

requirements.subject: ent:action-statement
requirements.canonical: The `action` statement has the syntax `action` "(" { ( FreeText | TemplateInstance ) [","] } ")".

requirements.subject: ent:action-statement
requirements.canonical: The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.original: External actions can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.

ambiguity.issue: The list omits the module control function, although table 16 and clause 26 allow `action` in control behaviour. Chosen reading: the list is not exhaustive. Also "test cases" is used where "testcases" (the language element) is meant.
readings: The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions, altsteps and the module control function.
The `action` statement MAY be used only in testcases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:action-statement
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language does not specify what is done to or by the SUT to trigger the external action; the `action` statement IS only an informal description of the required action.
requirements.original: There is no specification of what is done to or by the SUT to trigger this action, only an informal description of the required action itself.

non_requirement.reason: motivation for external actions (missing or unknown SUT interfaces)
motivation: actions required from test executing personnel
only the general static rules of clause 5 and table 16 apply; no own restriction
